text: 🇲🇽🎨 A new national museum with no director — run by the artisans themselves. "This museum has no director; it is run by a council that makes decisions together with artisans and specialist craftspeople." — Claudia Curiel, Culture Secretary, on the Textile Museum The Museo Textil, dedicated to indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples, opened beside the Templo Mayor: twelve halls, interactive spaces and workshops. Museum and archaeological-site attendance rose 18% during the Social World Cup.

🇲🇽🌎 "I don't agree with the tariffs — but that doesn't mean we stop talking." "I don't agree with the tariffs, but that doesn't mean we interrupt the talks or stop seeking the best agreement." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on US trade relations She holds the line against the tariffs while keeping the door open. As proof of collaboration, US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins visits Saturday to open a sterile-fly plant in Chiapas against the screwworm. The T-MEC review resumes in July.

🚨🇲🇽 "What we don't agree with is interference in Mexico's affairs." "We are very clear about what we do not agree with: interference in Mexico's internal affairs." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on US pressure Asked about the US ultraright, Sheinbaum said Mexico does not want to be used in the November US election campaign. Cooperation and dialogue, yes — interference in Mexico's internal affairs, no.

🇲🇽🌎 "The self-determination of peoples, and peace." "The self-determination of peoples, and peace." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on Mexican foreign policy Describing her talk with Spain's King, Sheinbaum named the principles that guide Mexico: the UN Charter, the self-determination of peoples, and peace — the same doctrine written into Article 89 of the Constitution that has steered Mexican diplomacy for a century.

🇲🇽🎨 The first thing Sheinbaum raised with Spain's King was Mexico's indigenous peoples. "The first topic I raised was the matter of the indigenous peoples, the original peoples, the importance they hold for Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on her meeting with Felipe VI At the June 25 meeting she opened by raising the original peoples and the pending apology for the abuses of the Conquest — a question, she said, of national identity, and of no to racism, no to classism, no to any form of discrimination.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 Mexico sends 250 troops and rescue dogs to earthquake-stricken Venezuela. "The Army and the Air Force, always first, helping the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the aid to Venezuela Two quakes (7.2 and 7.5) struck Yaracuy on June 24; the toll passed 920. Mexico deployed 250 soldiers, 18 search-and-rescue dogs and medical supplies. Sheinbaum spoke with VP Delcy Rodríguez on June 26 to coordinate. Aid sent without conditions.

🇲🇽📉 MEXICO BEAT THE US ON INFLATION — AND DID IT WITH FUEL SUBSIDIES

Mexico's annual inflation fell to 3.55% in the first half of June, its lowest since October and below the 3.72% analysts expected. Across the border, US inflation just climbed to 4.1% — a three-year high — as Middle East war drove gasoline up. The difference is policy: Mexico caps fuel prices and runs fiscal stimulus on gasoline to shield families, while Washington lets the market pass war costs straight to consumers. Six straight fortnights of falling prices in Mexico; a three-year peak in the US.

🇲🇽⚡ SHEINBAUM: "ENERGY PRODUCTION MUST GUARANTEE NATIONAL SOVEREIGNTY"

President Sheinbaum inaugurated a new CFE combined-cycle plant in Mexicali, adding 653 MW to the national grid and declaring that "energy production must guarantee national sovereignty." It's one piece of a six-year plan to add 32,000 MW — 22,000 of them renewable — while raising the state utility CFE's share of generation from 54% to 60%. Baja California alone is receiving over 73.9 billion pesos in energy investment, plus a 1.485-billion-peso subsidy holding down summer electricity bills for 1.37 million people.

🇲🇽✊ MEXICO'S NATIONAL LOTTERY HONORS THE BATTLE THAT BROKE A DICTATORSHIP

112 years ago, on June 23, 1914, Francisco Villa's División del Norte — alongside General Felipe Ángeles and Pánfilo Natera — stormed Zacatecas and shattered the army of usurper Victoriano Huerta, hastening the dictator's collapse. Mexico's National Lottery is now dedicating its Sorteo Mayor to that battle. Its director, Olivia Salomón, said the Toma de Zacatecas "transcended the military sphere to become a symbol of resistance and transformation."

🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO SENDS 250 TROOPS AND RESCUE TEAMS TO EARTHQUAKE-HIT VENEZUELA

While Washington tightens sanctions on Caracas, Mexico sends rescuers. President Sheinbaum dispatched 250 Defense Ministry personnel, four aircraft, drones, canine units and medical equipment to Venezuela after twin earthquakes (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5) killed at least 188 people on June 24. "There are no reports of affected, injured or deceased Mexican citizens," she confirmed — the mission is pure solidarity with a neighbor in mourning.
